notes: §1985:VI.6.4.2 GR3: "If, after radix point alignment, the absolute value of a result exceeds the largest value that can be contained in the associated resultant identifier, a size error condition exists", for a BINARY item "the maximum value implied by the associated decimal PICTURE character-string", and "If the ROUNDED phrase is specified, rounding takes place before checking for size error"; the paragraphs under it keep an affected resultant unchanged under ON SIZE ERROR, store the others, run the phrase after the arithmetic, skip NOT ON SIZE ERROR on a size error, and defer the phrase of ADD or SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING "until all of the individual additions or subtractions are completed". StoreArith lands every resultant of a statement with a size-error phrase through CobolNum.TryStore, which rescales to the receiver's scale with the receiver's rounding first and then refuses a value of more digits than the PICTURE holds, by decimal digit count for DISPLAY, PACKED-DECIMAL, COMP and BINARY alike (the binary-container limit is the arm of COMP-5 and the BINARY-CHAR family, which are not 1985 usages); a numeric-edited resultant asks the same of CobolEdit.TryFormat. GuardedStore gives each resultant its own guarded store, so one refusal leaves that item unchanged and the rest stored, and EmitArith runs ON SIZE ERROR or NOT ON SIZE ERROR once after all of them, which CorrespondingEmitter.Emit shares pair by pair. Without a phrase the 1985 result is undefined and control goes on: EmitArith takes the unchecked store whenever EnabledSizeNames is empty, and at 85 it always is (>>TURN is refused, COBOL0900), so 2023's EC-SIZE termination is unreachable. Probed at --std 85: S99 BINARY takes the size error at +100 and -100 and stores -99; 9(4) BINARY at 10000; COMP, PACKED-DECIMAL and a negative DISPLAY product at 100; 9.95 ROUNDED into 9V9 is a size error while 9.94 ROUNDED and 9.99 truncated are not; PIC 99PP takes 9950 ROUNDED and 10000 as size errors and 9949 ROUNDED not; PIC PP99 at .0100; DIVIDE GIVING two receivers both too small leaves both unchanged; COMPUTE D1 D2 leaves the 2-digit item and stores the 3-digit one; a numeric-edited Z9.9 receiver takes 99.95 ROUNDED as a size error; ON SIZE ERROR GO TO leaves the statement; a multi-statement imperative runs whole and then passes END-ADD; with no ON phrase NOT ON SIZE ERROR is skipped and execution continues. The witness runs ADD with two receivers (one unchanged, one stored), a BINARY PIC 99 receiver at 110, ROUNDED carrying 99.6 past 99, NOT ON SIZE ERROR without a size error, and ADD CORRESPONDING whose phrase sees the second pair already stored.

next.reason: The detection rule, ROUNDED-before-check, the ON SIZE ERROR path (resultants unchanged, control to the imperative, NOT SIZE ERROR ignored) and the CORRESPONDING timing are kept (§2023:14.7.5 GR3 'further from zero than permitted for the associated resultant data item'; §2023:14.7.6 'the imperative-statement in the SIZE ERROR phrase is executed after all of the implied statements are completed'). The no-phrase case differs: §1985:VI.6.4.2 GR3 'the values of the affected resultant identifiers are undefined' and control goes to the end of the statement, while 2023 sets 'the EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION exception condition is set to exist' and 'processing proceeds as specified in 14.6.13.1.3, Fatal exception conditions' (§2023:14.7.5): run unit 'terminated abnormally' when checking is enabled (§2023:14.6.13.1.3 GR7), implementor-defined continuation when it is not (§2023:14.6.13.1.3 GR8). 2023 also adds a nearer-to-zero size error (§2023:14.7.5 GR4), reachable only under ROUNDED MODE IS PROHIBITED.
